dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef001
dependency_coverage.meaning: Projects the cell-region function from the partition: each cell c is assigned a subset R_c of Point.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Determines the sets whose measures, restricted integrals, and averages occur.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef002
dependency_coverage.meaning: The mesh structure described by D014: a measurable cell partition, a nonempty interface type, distinct left and right cells for each interface, and an interface point in the domain and in both adjacent cell closures.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Restricts the quantified mesh and supplies all geometric and incidence data used by the proposition.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef003
dependency_coverage.meaning: Projects the function assigning a left cell L_i to each interface i.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Selects the first numerical-flux argument and the positive incidence contribution.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef004
dependency_coverage.meaning: Projects the function assigning a right cell R_i to each interface i.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Selects the second numerical-flux argument and the negative incidence contribution.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef005
dependency_coverage.meaning: Projects the underlying cell partition from the mesh.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Makes the partition domain, regions, and partition constraints part of the mesh data.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef006
dependency_coverage.meaning: For a measure μ, region S, field u, and value a, asserts μ(S) ≠ 0, μ(S) ≠ ∞, integrability of u on S, and a = LocalDef015 μ S u, all conjunctively.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The cell-average conclusion repeats the volume and integrability assumptions and identifies each average with its defining normalized integral.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef007
dependency_coverage.meaning: At interface i, evaluates the physical flux function at the field value at its designated point: f(u(p_i)).
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The approximation compares numerical flux with a point evaluation, not an interface integral or a trace.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef008
dependency_coverage.meaning: For a finite cell set S and interface flux F, returns the sum over all interfaces i of (F_i if L_i ∈ S, otherwise 0) minus (F_i if R_i ∈ S, otherwise 0).
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Defines the aggregate flux term in the finite-set balance; interfaces with both endpoints in S cancel.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef009
dependency_coverage.meaning: Assigns to each cell c the normalized restricted integral LocalDef015 μ R_c u.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Fixes the initial cell averages used in the flux approximation and both balance equations.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef010
dependency_coverage.meaning: For cell c, sums over all interfaces i the contribution (F_i if L_i = c, otherwise 0) minus (F_i if R_i = c, otherwise 0).
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Defines the signed cell flux subtracted, after multiplication by the time increment, in the local balance.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef011
dependency_coverage.meaning: For cell values a and a binary numerical-flux function g, assigns interface i the value g(a(L_i), a(R_i)).
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: All numerical interface fluxes use the same ordered pair rule applied to the initial averages.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef012
dependency_coverage.meaning: The partition structure described by D017: a domain, a cell-region function, nonempty Cell, measurable pairwise disjoint cell regions, and exact coverage of the domain.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Provides structural hypotheses on the regions without asserting that Cell is finite.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef013
dependency_coverage.meaning: Projects the designated point p_i of each interface.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Determines where the field is evaluated for the physical-flux comparison.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef014
dependency_coverage.meaning: Constructs a mesh from a partition, nonempty Interface, maps L and R with L_i ≠ R_i for every i, and points p_i lying in the partition domain and in the closures of both corresponding regions.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Encodes nonempty interfaces, distinct adjacent cells, and closure incidence; it does not encode interface areas, normals, or boundary faces.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef015
dependency_coverage.meaning: Returns ((μ(S)).toReal)⁻¹ • integral(μ restricted to S, u), using real scalar multiplication.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Normalizes the supplied integral by real cell volume. The assumptions make this volume finite and strictly positive; the integral's hidden implementation remains the limitation identified at D096.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef016
dependency_coverage.meaning: Projects the domain subset from a partition.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The domain is exactly covered by cell regions and contains every designated interface point.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef017
dependency_coverage.meaning: Constructs a partition with nonempty Cell, measurable regions, disjoint regions for distinct cells, and x ∈ domain if and only if some cell region contains x.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Imposes exact set-theoretic partition conditions, rather than only almost-everywhere coverage or disjointness.

binders: Universally quantify over types Cell, Interface, Point, and E in arbitrary universes.
Point has a measurable-space structure and a topological-space structure, with no stated compatibility condition.
Interface has a finite enumeration, Cell has decidable equality, and E is a real normed vector space, not assumed complete.
Universally quantify over a mesh of the specified structure and a measure μ on Point.
Universally quantify over a field u : Point → E, a physical-flux function f : E → E, and an ordered binary numerical-flux function g : E → E → E.
Universally quantify over real numbers t₀ = timeStart, t₁ = timeEnd, and ε = fluxTolerance.

The conclusion existentially quantifies one function b : Cell → E after all these inputs and assumptions. Both its cellwise balance and its finite-set balance must hold simultaneously; b is chosen independently of the subsequently quantified finite cell set.
hypotheses: The mesh includes a domain Ω and regions C_c for c ∈ Cell. Cell is nonempty, every C_c is measurable, distinct cell regions are disjoint, and x ∈ Ω if and only if there exists c with x ∈ C_c.
Interface is nonempty. Each interface i has cells L_i and R_i with L_i ≠ R_i and a point p_i ∈ Ω ∩ closure(C_{L_i}) ∩ closure(C_{R_i}).
For every cell c, u is integrable with respect to μ restricted to C_c.
For every interface i, dist(g(a_{L_i}, a_{R_i}), f(u(p_i))) < ε, where a_c is the fixed normalized integral defined below.
conclusions: Δt = t₁ − t₀ is strictly positive.
For every cell c, μ(C_c) ≠ 0, μ(C_c) ≠ ∞, u is integrable on C_c, and a_c = v_c⁻¹ • I_c, all conjunctively.
For every interface i, F_i = g(a_{L_i}, a_{R_i}) and dist(F_i, f(u(p_i))) < ε, both conjunctively.
There exists one b : Cell → E such that, for every cell c, v_c • b_c = v_c • a_c − Δt • Q_c.
For that same b and every finite set S of cells, Σ_{c∈S} v_c • b_c = (Σ_{c∈S} v_c • a_c) − Δt • B_S.
mathematical_definitions: Ω is the partition domain and C_c is the measurable region assigned to cell c.
L_i and R_i are the ordered left and right cells of interface i, and p_i is its designated point.
v_c = (μ(C_c)).toReal. The volume hypotheses imply that v_c is a finite strictly positive real number.
I_c = MeasureTheory.integral(μ restricted to C_c, u), retaining the integral operation supplied in the dossier; conventionally this is written ∫_{C_c} u dμ.
a_c = v_c⁻¹ • I_c, where • denotes real scalar multiplication on E.
F_i = g(a_{L_i}, a_{R_i}) and P_i = f(u(p_i)); both are elements of E.
Q_c = Σ_{i∈Interface} ((if L_i = c then F_i else 0_E) − (if R_i = c then F_i else 0_E)).
B_S = Σ_{i∈Interface} ((if L_i ∈ S then F_i else 0_E) − (if R_i ∈ S then F_i else 0_E)).
All interface sums are over the entire finite interface type. All sums indexed by S are finite sums without repetitions.
The distance on E is its norm-induced distance, so dist(F_i, P_i) = ‖F_i − P_i‖.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every measurable and topological point space, real normed vector space E, and mesh consisting of a nonempty measurable disjoint partition of a domain together with finitely many nonempty interfaces joining distinct cells at designated common-closure points, take a measure μ, field u, physical-flux map f, numerical-flux map g, and real times t₀ < t₁ with positive tolerance ε. Suppose every cell has nonzero finite measure, u is integrable on every cell, and the numerical flux computed from its two initial normalized cell integrals is within strict distance ε of f evaluated at u at the designated interface point. Then the time increment and tolerance are positive, each initial average satisfies the stated positive-finite-volume and integrability conditions and equals its defining normalized integral, and each numerical interface flux equals its defining ordered two-cell expression and satisfies the assumed error bound. Moreover, there exists a single assignment b of updated vectors to all cells whose volume-weighted value in each cell equals its initial volume-weighted value minus the time increment times the signed sum of numerical interface fluxes, positive for left incidence and negative for right incidence. The same assignment satisfies, for every finite set of cells, the corresponding summed balance with the aggregate flux B_S, in which contributions from interfaces with both adjacent cells selected cancel.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: Cell is not assumed finite or countable. Only Interface is finite, and the aggregate conclusion concerns finite cell sets; it does not assert an infinite-sum conservation law.

The mesh prevents empty-interface and empty-cell vacuity. Its nonempty interface type and distinct endpoints force at least two cells, and its interface-point map forces Point and the domain to be nonempty.
The finite-set conclusion includes S = ∅, for which the equation is the trivial zero equality.

The theorem is conditional on the flux approximation for the chosen field, flux maps, mesh, and tolerance. It does not construct a flux satisfying that bound or establish the bound from consistency or regularity assumptions.
Every cell measure must be nonzero and finite. This excludes degeneracy in the scalar volume factors, but there is no uniform lower or upper bound on volumes.
The mesh regions are exactly disjoint and cover exactly the domain. The hypotheses do not assert that the domain is measurable when Cell is an arbitrary possibly uncountable type.
The topology of Point need not be related to its sigma-algebra, and μ need not be a geometric volume measure. No Euclidean geometry, dimensionality, regular cell shape, or metric on Point is assumed.

Interfaces have designated points and two distinct cells, but no interface regions, areas, normal vectors, orientation geometry beyond left/right incidence, or completeness condition listing all geometric contacts. Different interfaces may share endpoints or points.
Every encoded interface has two cells. There is no separate exterior-boundary flux object or boundary condition.

The physical comparison uses u(p_i) pointwise. Cellwise integrability does not determine these point values from an almost-everywhere equivalence class, and the proposition asserts no traces or continuity.
The field and flux maps have no time argument. The real times enter the balances only through their difference; no time-dependent conservation equation or time integral is encoded.
No continuity, Lipschitz property, monotonicity, symmetry, antisymmetry, or consistency identity such as g(z, z) = f(z) is imposed on the flux maps.

The witness b is an arbitrary E-valued cell assignment satisfying algebraic equations. No updated spatial field is supplied whose cell integrals realize b, and no stability, positivity preservation, convergence, or error bound for b is asserted.
The existential statement does not explicitly claim uniqueness, although the positive real volume factors make the cellwise equations determine b_c algebraically.

The approximation and average-identification portions of the conclusion repeat assumptions and definitions. The balance existence itself is an algebraic update condition on the fixed initial averages and interface fluxes.

E is not assumed complete or nontrivial. A trivial vector space makes flux distances and vector balances degenerate; the hidden implementation of integration for incomplete spaces is not exposed by the dossier.
ambiguities: D096 exposes MeasureTheory.integral only as MeasureTheory.wrapped✝.1. Consequently, the packet does not reveal its defining construction or its totalization behavior when E is incomplete. The translation precisely preserves that supplied integral operation, but an unconditional identification with a conventionally defined E-valued Bochner integral for all quantified E would require additional semantic information.
